Created by combining {{D|Heat}} and {{D|Toxin}} damage. {{D|Gas}} produces gas clouds that deal damage to all enemies within a 3 meter radius for a short duration.|In-game Description}} {{D|Gas}} '''Damage''' is one of the six secondary elemental damage types, composed of {{D|Heat}} and {{D|Toxin}} elements. Deals increased damage to {{D|Infested Deimos}} and {{D|Techrot}} enemies but reduced damage against {{D|Scaldra}} enemies. Its [[Status Effect]] creates a damaging cloud that deals {{D|Gas}} [[Damage over Time]]. ==[[Status Effect]]s== ===General=== The status effect of {{D|Gas}} damage is '''Gas Cloud'''. It produces a gas cloud that deals a tick of damage each second to all enemies within a '''3'''-meter radius; subsequent procs increase the radius by '''0.3''' meters up to '''6 '''meters in total after '''10''' stacks. The cloud has a '''6''' second duration. Each tick deals {{D|Gas}} damage equal to: : { \begin{aligned} \text{Gas Proc Damage per Tick} &= 0.5 \times \text{Modded Base Damage} \\ &\qquad \times (1 + \text{Gas Damage Bonuses}) \\ &\qquad \times (1 + \text{Faction Damage Bonuses}) \\ &\qquad \times (1 + \text{Status Damage Bonuses}) \\ &\qquad \times \text{Additional Multipliers} \end{aligned} } ::''Gas Damage Bonuses include {{M|Valence Formation}}.'' ::''Additional Multipliers include modded critical multiplier on [[Critical Hit]] and multipliers on [[Enemy Body Parts]]; these stack multiplicatively with each other.'' :Modded Base Damage is not the same as normal damage calculations, ignoring physical and elemental damage bonuses and calculated as: :: { \begin{aligned} \text{Modded Base Damage} &= \text{Base Damage} \times (1 + \text{Base Damage Bonuses}) \times (1 + \text{Faction Damage Bonuses}) \end{aligned} } As can be seen from the formula, tick damage scales with {{D|Gas}} mods ({{D|Heat}} and {{D|Toxin}} mods have no effect). Up to '''10''' instances of the effect can stack on the same target, with each instance having its own timer. Any instances after the 10th will replace the oldest instance. The Gas Cloud is able to hit heads and other [[Enemy Body Parts|body parts]] by itself. However, the Gas Cloud itself has a '''1x''' damage bonus when headshotting. This can be increased with the use of mods such as {{M|Target Acquired}}, zoom bonuses on some [[Sniper Rifle|sniper rifles]], or {{Arcane|Primary Deadhead}}/{{Arcane|Secondary Deadhead}}. Example 1 ({{D|Heat}} and {{D|Toxin}} mods), tick damage for a weapon with an innate 180 damage, {{M|Hornet Strike}}, {{M|Scorch}}, {{M|Pathogen Rounds}}, {{M|Expel Grineer}}, and {{M|Pistol Elementalist}} will be: :Modded Base Damage = {{Math|180 {{mul}} (1 + 2.2) {{mul}} (1 + 0.3)|t=y|bf-a=y}} :'''Tick Damage''' = {{Math|0.5 {{mul}} 748.8 {{mul}} (1 + 0.3) {{mul}} (1 + 0.9)|t=y|bf-a=y}} Example 2 ({{D|Gas}} mod), tick damage for the {{Weapon|Vesper 77}} with {{M|Hornet Strike}}, {{M|Leaded Gas}}, {{M|Expel Grineer}}, and {{M|Pistol Elementalist}} will be: :Modded Base Damage = {{Math|180 {{mul}} (1 + 2.2) {{mul}} (1 + 0.3)|t=y|bf-a=y}} :'''Tick Damage''' = {{Math|0.5 {{mul}} 748.8 {{mul}} (1 + 3) {{mul}} (1 + 0.3) {{mul}} (1 + 0.9)|t=y|bf-a=y}} As can be seen in the above calculations for tick damage, Faction Damage is applied twice, making their effective bonus {{MathText|{{eql}} (1 + Faction Damage bonus)2}}. Which is +69% for the 30% Faction Damage mods and +140.25% for the 55% Primed Faction Damage mods. If the host target dies, {{D|Gas}} will continue to tick damage on all enemies caught in the host's radius for its remaining duration. A {{D|Gas}} proc briefly creates a dark green cloud on the afflicted. {| class="wikitable" |+ Gas tick damage and proc duration |- ! {{Top|Lotus|Tenno|Tenno|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|Daikyu takes great strength to draw back, but provides added power and range to every shot.}} The '''Daikyu''' is an asymmetrical bow of {{Faction|Tenno}} design and origin. It has larger damage, [[status chance]] and increased [[Projectile Speed]] compared to the other bows, as well as high [[critical chance]], but takes longer to fully draw and cannot be released early for decreased damage. ==Characteristics== *This weapon primarily deals {{D|Puncture}} damage. *Guaranteed {{D|Impact}} proc. **Can fully benefit of {{M|Internal Bleeding}}. *Charged shots have an innate 3 meter [[punch through]], the highest of all bows. **As it can only be fired when fully charged, shots will always have the [[punch through]]. *On kill, bodies will follow the arrow that killed them, damaging anyone in their path and pinning the corpse to walls. *Medium-to-high [[zoom]] level when aiming. *Can equip the bow-exclusive {{M|Thunderbolt}} mod, and the Daikyu-exclusive {{M|Spring-Loaded Broadhead}} and {{M|Amalgam Daikyu Target Acquired}} mods. *[[Fire rate]] mods apply double their bonuses. *Innate {{Pol|Madurai}} polarity. {{Advantages|class=Bow| *Highest shot base damage of all bows. (without counting the AOE effect of {{Weapon|Proboscis Cernos}},{{Weapon|Kuva Bramma}}, and {{Weapon|Lenz}}) *Second highest [[status chance]] of all bows, behind {{Weapon|Mutalist Cernos}}. *Second fastest [[Projectile Speed]] of all primary weapons, behind {{Weapon|Lanka}}. *Fastest [[Projectile Speed]] of all bows. **Arrows have low arc due to flight speed. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Bow| *Second slowest [[Fire Rate|charge speed]] of all bows, after {{Weapon|Lenz}}. **Cannot be fired at partial charge. *Arrows have travel time with slight arcing. }} {{WeaponComparison|Daikyu Prime}} ==Acquisition== The Daikyu's blueprint can be [[research]]ed from the [[Research/Tenno Lab|Tenno Lab]] in the [[dojo]]. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} This weapon can be sold for {{cc|7,500}}. ==Notes== *The Daikyu does not have a quick fire option, nor can it be fired at partial charge - it must be fully charged before it can be fired. **The weapon's charge, both in its draw phase and its hold phase, can be cancelled by performing actions that will break normal weapon charges, such as pressing reload, rolling, or switching to another weapon. *The Daikyu reportedly does not benefit from multiplicative gun CO from Galvanized Aptitude. Instead, it acts the same as damage mods like Serration, Heavy Caliber, or gun Arcanes like Primary Merciless. ==Tips== *This weapon is perfect for {{M|Internal Bleeding}}: with the guaranteed {{D|Impact}} proc and slow fire rate, each arrow has 70% chance to apply bleed. **With {{M|Internal Bleeding}} + {{M|Vile Acceleration}} + {{M|Critical Delay}}, the weapon has guaranteed crit (120%), a fast charge time (0.42s), and is still just above the threshold to have 70% proc rate from Internal Bleeding. * The increased [[Projectile Speed]] and subsequent low arc makes it much easier to achieve headshots and hit enemies at very long ranges. * {{M|Speed Trigger}}, ({{M|Primed Shred|Primed}}) {{M|Shred}}, {{M|Vigilante Fervor}} and {{M|Vile Acceleration}} can be used individually or in combination to speed up the Daikyu's draw speed. ==Trivia== *The ''daikyū'' (大弓) is one of two variants of the Japanese asymmetrical ''[[wikipedia:Yumi|yumi]]'' bow. Read as "big bow" or "Longbow", the ''daikyū'' is the larger variant to the smaller ''hankyū'' (半弓; lit. "half bow"). *The mechanics of this bow appear to be heavily based on the principles of ''[[wikipedia:Kyūdō|Kyūdō]]'', the practice of Japanese archery. By taking one's time and adopting proper shooting posture and form, the arrow is assured to hit its mark. *The Codex description mentions great strength required to draw the Daikyu, which may refer to its prolonged drawing time. *The Daikyu was the first bow that has a completely compact, collapsible form when holstered. It folds into three pieces: its two arms and the grip, creating a U-shape as the arms point upward on the player's back. The {{Weapon|Lenz}} would follow as the second, folding in a similar manner. ==Media== Update16_5_Day3Weapons-AsymmetricalBow.jpg|Preview image of the Daikyu. {{Top|Enemy|Corpus|Corpus|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|Forgo ammunition with the regenerating energy disc in this plasma throwing pistol.}} The '''Cycron''' is a {{Faction|Corpus}} plasma {{D|Radiation}} beam pistol with a battery that automatically regenerates ammo after the user stops firing for a second. This weapon can be sold for {{cc|5,000}}. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals primarily {{D|Radiation}} damage. *Damage ramps up from 30% to 100% over 0.6 seconds when firing. After firing stops for 0.8 seconds, the damage decays back to 30% over 2 seconds. *Does not use ammo pickups; ammo regenerates over time. **Has a '''1''' second delay after the weapon stops firing before regenerating ammo. ***Regenerates '''40''' ammo per second; takes '''1''' second to regenerate a fully depleted battery. **Does not benefit from mods that increase [[Ammo#Ammo Maximum|maximum ammo]], due to lack of an ammo pool. **Does not benefit from reload-triggered mods such as {{M|Pressurized Magazine}}. *Innate 1 meter [[punch through]]. {{Advantages|class=Pistol|trigger=Held| *Fourth highest [[status chance]] of all continuous secondaries, behind the {{Weapon|Tenet Cycron}}, {{Weapon|Embolist}} and {{Weapon|Kuva Nukor}}. *Pinpoint [[accuracy]]. **{{M|Magnum Force}}'s accuracy penalty is minimal on this weapon. *Consumes 0.5 ammo per tick of damage. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Pistol|trigger=Held| *Range limited to 24 meters. }} {{WeaponComparison|Tenet Cycron}} ==Acquisition== The Cycron's blueprint can be [[research]]ed from the [[Research/Energy Lab|Energy Lab]] in the [[dojo]]. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} ==Notes== *Similar to [[Rampart]]s and all [[Archgun]]s, ammo starts to automatically regenerate after '''1''' seconds of not firing the weapon. This regeneration delay is affected by reload speed mods like {{M|Quickdraw}} and {{M|Stunning Speed}}. The regeneration rate is 40 ammo per second. **The reload speed can also be increased passively with {{WF|Chroma}}, by using a Toxin-based {{A|Elemental Ward}} or being under the effect of {{A|Speed}} or {{A|Penance}}. *The Cycron's beam has a maximum range of '''24''' meters. **This makes the Cycron an excellent weapon for multiple elemental builds as its innate Radiation status and a high status chance for other elemental procs allow it to take down enemies quickly with procs alone. *Even if equipped with {{M|Eject Magazine}}, the Cycron will '''not''' bypass its 1-second regeneration delay when holstered. Instead, the mod will simply accelerate the rate at which ammo is regenerated when holstered, once the delay is over. *Because the 40 shots count as part of a single magazine rather than an ammo pool, mods like {{M|Trick Mag}} have no effect. ==Trivia== *The Cycron is the first weapon to use the ammo regeneration mechanic outside of [[Archwing]]. *Corpus script {{CorpusScript|BCDE KLMNO VW YZ}} is written on the side of the gun, spelling "BCDE KLMNO VW YZ". ==Media== CycronBanner.png|Promotional banner CycronConcept1.jpg|Concept art CycronConcept2.jpg|Concept art CycronConcept3.jpg|Concept art CycronConcept4.jpg|Concept art CycronConcept5.jpg|Concept art CycronConcept6.jpg|Concept art {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|Ei66Vt5G96s|size=300px}} }} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|33}} *The following weapons can now be found in their corresponding categories in the Arsenal when searching using the tag “Battery”: **Cycron {{ver|32.0.2}} ;Ammo Changes & Review: When we were reviewing ammo acquisition as a whole for Update 32, we felt weapons with Ammo Regen Rate Overrides, or “Battery,” in particular, needed a place within the ecosystem of change we had established. The following explains how a certain amount of damage of one or more damage types turns into actual inflicted damage to a target, considering [[Damage Type Modifier]]s.

[[Armor]], [[Damage Reduction]], [[Faction Damage Bonus]], [[Enemy Body Parts]], [[critical hit]], [[Stealth Damage Bonus]], as well as Warframe [[debuffs]], are ignored in this article since all of these are independent of damage types.

===Quantization===
{{UpdateMe|Conflicting info:
*"Damage mods such as {{M|Hornet Strike}}, [[Faction Damage Bonus]] such as {{M|Bane of Grineer}}, and any other multipliers only multiply final quantized values and do not affect the scale or damage composition."
*"Applying {{M|Serration|+Damage}}, {{M|Bane of Grineer|+Faction}} or any other non-elemental bonus multiplies both the base value of rounding numerator and Scale of rounding denominator, and therefore is a simple multiplier to any quantized total."
}}
'''Dealing damage is [[wikipedia:Quantization|quantized]].''' Meaning, rather than the damage being applied smoothly, physical and elemental damages round to the nearest multiple of 1/32nd of their attack's base damage, before being multiplied further.<ref>{{Ref|title=Internal rounding leading to unintended applied damage|author= Theroxenes|year=2018|month=3|day=2|publisher=Warframe Forums|url=https://forums.warframe.com/topic/928927-internal-rounding-leading-to-unintended-applied-damage/|access-date=2022-09-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220919171910/https://forums.warframe.com/topic/928927-internal-rounding-leading-to-unintended-applied-damage/|archive-date=2022-09-19}}</ref><ref>{{Ref|title=Internal damage quantization or: Another way the arsenal is lying to you.|author=Theroxenes|year=2018|month=2|day=28|publisher=Reddit|url=https://www.reddit.com/r/Warframe/comments/809yaa/internal_damage_quantization_or_another_way_the/|access-date=2022-09-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211124174002/https://www.reddit.com/r/Warframe/comments/809yaa/internal_damage_quantization_or_another_way_the/|archive-date=2021-11-24}}</ref> By using this method of quantization, the precision of data is reduced, thereby saving storage space and improving the efficiency of computer operations. Rather than communicating a lengthy integer of each element's value, only one "Total" integer along with short representative multiples of 1/32nd need to be communicated.

<math>
{
\text{Scale} = \frac{\text{Modded Base Damage}}{32}
}
</math>

For each damage type, first express its value as a signed proportion of the modded base damage:

<math>
x = \frac{\text{Total Damage Type Value}}{\text{Modded Base Damage}}
</math>

The exact quantization rule is:

<math>
\operatorname{Quantized}(x)
= \operatorname{sign}(x) \times \frac{\left\lfloor |x| \times 32 + 0.5 \right\rfloor}{32}
</math>

The quantized damage type value is then:

<math>
\text{Quantized Damage Type Value}
= \operatorname{Quantized}(x) \times \text{Modded Base Damage}
</math>

For non-negative values, this is equivalent to dividing the damage type value by the scale, applying <math>\left\lfloor y+0.5\right\rfloor</math>, and multiplying by the scale. For negative values, the same operation is applied to the absolute magnitude before restoring the sign. This quantized value is used in mission damage calculations. The final damage seen in damage pop-ups is further rounded to a whole number.

# For example, if you have a weapon with a listed damage distribution of 30 {{D|Impact}}, 30 {{D|Puncture}}, and 40 {{D|Slash}}, the total damage is '''100'''.
# The value of a scale will then be {{Math|100 {{div}} 32|t=y|bf-a=y}}.
# The amount of {{D|Impact}} damage dealt by the weapon will then be {{Math|30 {{div}} 3.125|t=y}} rounded to the nearest whole number, multiplied by the scale: {{Math|10 {{mul}} 3.125|t=y|bf-a=y}}.  This process is applied to {{D|Puncture}} and {{D|Slash}} as well, yielding '''31.25''' and '''40.625''' respectively.
# As such, when damaging a {{E|Charger}}, which has a +50% bonus to {{D|Slash}} damage due to having {{D|Infested}} health, the total damage dealt to the Charger will then be {{Math|31.25 + 31.25 + 40.625 {{mul}} (1 + 50%)|t=y|bf-a=y}} (the game will display the rounded value of {{Math|31.25 + 31.25 + 40.625 {{mul}} (1 + 50%)|round=1}}). 

*Note that while sometimes the weapon's total damage after the conversion remains the same, mixed-type weapon damage is frequently '''gained''' or '''lost''' by the conversion.

====Adding Physical and/or Elemental Mods/Bonuses====
If a physical or elemental mod is applied, their bonuses are also quantized.
# The value of the example scale will still be {{Math|100 / 32|t=y|bf-a=y}}. Elemental and Physical bonuses do not affect the scale.
# If {{M|Maim}} was used, for example, the {{D|Slash}} damage on the weapon after quantization would be round(40 {{mul}} (1 + {{M|Maim|1.2}}) {{div}} 3.125) {{mul}} 3.125 = '''87.5'''.
# The damage distribution would then be '''31.25''' {{D|Impact}}, '''31.25''' {{D|Puncture}}, and '''87.5''' {{D|Slash}}.
# Elemental bonuses calculate using the '''full''' base damage, are rounded to the nearest 1/32nd of the base damage and added to the total.
# Elements formed by a sum of mods and bonuses quantize their sum alone. For example, if 90% {{D|Cold}} combined with 90% {{D|Toxin}}, or 90% modded {{D|Radiation}} combined with 90% of {{M|Smite Infusion}}, these types would count separately as a sum of their final element (180% {{D|Viral}}, or 180% {{D|Radiation}}), each rounded to the nearest 1/32 of base damage, and finally added to the quantized total.

====Summary====
Calculating damage with quantization can be simplified to the following steps:
#Get Scale
#Quantize Physical and Elemental Damage
#Add quantized values together
#Apply all other multipliers such as [[Damage Type Modifier]]

====Trivia====
* [[Hitscan]] weapons do not quantize against {{D|Object}} health such as [[Nullifier Bubble]]s and {{WF|Zephyr}} {{A|Tornado}}. [[Projectile]]s however will be quantized. This characteristic has been used to determine damage compositions not disclosed in-game, so they can be presented here in the wiki.
* [[Melee]] weapons with very low {{D|Impact}} damage relative to other damage types will not trigger {{M|Shattering Impact}} due to quantization of the {{D|Impact}} damage value to 0. {{Weapon|Galatine}} for example has 2.5% {{D|Impact}} damage.
* Here is a comparison of space savings for using non-quantized vs. quantized values. As more damage types are present on the attack, the greater the space saving:
** If we use 64-bit floating-point values for each damage type (e.g. {{D|Impact}} = 30, {{D|Puncture}} = 30, {{D|Slash}} = 40), that's 3 × 64 bits = 192 bits
** If we use one 64-bit floating-point value for the total damage and a smaller 16-bit floating-point value for each damage type's scale (e.g. Total = 100, {{D|Impact}} = 9.6, {{D|Puncture}} = 9.6, {{D|Slash}} = 12.8), that's 64 bits + (3 × 16 bits) = 112 bits. Almost a 42% size reduction with the tradeoff of clients needing to recompute the damage and losing some precision!

===Unarmored Enemies===
Against '''unarmored''' enemies or when applying {{D|True}} damage, the formula is simply:

<math>
{
\text{Inflicted Damage} = \text{Starting Damage} (1 + \text{Health-type Modifier})
}
</math>

*'''Inflicted Damage (ID)''' is the final damage result of a particular damage type.
*'''Starting Damage (SD)''' is the initial damage value of a particular damage type, modded or not.
*'''Health-type Modifier (HM)''' is the damage modifier against that health type (may be shields or health).

<hr />
To make it independent from the amount of base damage:

<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Damage Modifier} &= 1 + \text{Health-type Modifier} \\
\text{Inflicted Damage} &= \text{Starting Damage} \times \text{Damage Modifier}
\end{aligned}
}
</math>

* '''Damage Modifier (DM)''' is the total damage modifier. An amount of damage of that type (SD) against that enemy will then always be multiplied with this factor (DM).

===Armored Enemies===
Against '''[[armor]]ed''' enemies, the formula is:

<math>
{
DM = 1 - 0.9 \cdot \sqrt\frac{{AR}}{2700}
}
</math>

Where in addition to the previous definitions, '''AR''' is the target's armor after all reductions from debuffs (e.g. {{M|Corrosive Projection}}, {{D|Corrosive}} status effects, and {{A|Terrify}}).

In the case of enemies who have both [[shields]] and armor, damage to shields is not mitigated by armor. Lastly, when {{D|Toxin}} damage is applied to a shielded target, generally the damage is applied directly to its health, not shields (i.e. it bypasses shields). Some special enemies like [[Treasurer]] or [[Hound]]s cannot have their shields bypassed with {{D|Toxin}} damage however.

The damage numbers displayed in the in-game [[arsenal]] calculate total weapon damage as such:

<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Arsenal Total Damage} &= \text{Base Damage} \\
&\quad  \times [ 1 + \text{Elemental Bonuses} \\
&\qquad + \text{Unmodded Impact Distribution} \times \text{Impact Bonuses} \\
&\qquad + \text{Unmodded Puncture Distribution} \times \text{Puncture Bonuses} \\
&\qquad + \text{Unmodded Slash Distribution} \times \text{Slash Bonuses} ] \\
&\quad \times ( 1 + \text{Damage Bonuses}) \\
&\quad \times [\text{Base Weapon Multishot} \times ( 1 + \text{Multishot Bonuses})]
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
This arsenal damage is the average non-crit damage per shot, without [[Faction Damage Bonus]]. 
*For melee weapons, remove multishot from the equation. It does not include Stance damage multipliers.

|}

===Gun Damage Per Second===
When comparing the performance of non-melee weapons, it may be useful to calculate their theoretical single-target damage per second (DPS) (without accounting for status effects) using the following formulas:

====Average Burst DPS====
Average burst DPS is the theoretical damage a player does in a very short burst of time, or an extended period of time if ignoring time spent reloading/not firing their weapon.

{| class="wikitable"
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Average Burst DPS} &= \text{Average Shot} \times \text{Effective Fire Rate}
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
Where effective fire rate calculations is dependent on trigger type. Arsenal Fire Rate stat ≠ actual rate of fire in-game
*Assumes that damage ramp up is at max for Continuous Weapons. In actual gameplay, reloading will reset/decay the damage ramp up so Burst DPS will be lower than theoretical calculations.
*Assumes fire rate is the arsenal value for Auto-Spooled trigger weapons.
|-
|}

{| class="wikitable"
|+ Effective Fire Rate formulas by Trigger Type
|-
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Effective Fire Rate}_\text{Auto, Auto-Spool, Semi, Duplex, Held} &= \text{Modded Fire Rate}
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
For Auto, Semi, Duplex, and Held trigger types, the modded Fire Rate is the effective Fire Rate.
*For Semi and Duplex trigger types, we assume the player is able to achieve the modded Fire Rate value via manual attack inputs.
*For Auto-Spool trigger types, we assume that the weapon is fully spooled to the arsenal Fire Rate value.
|-
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Effective Fire Rate}_\text{Charge} &= \frac{ 1 }{ \text{Modded Charge Time} + \frac{ 1 }{ \text{Modded Fire Rate} } }
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
For Charge trigger types, the lower the [[Fire Rate]], the more delay between charge shots. If attack is not a Charge trigger type (Modded Charge Time = 0), then Effective Fire Rate = Modded Fire Rate. We assume the player immediately lets go for the attack key on full charge and doesn't delay the attack.
|-
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Effective Fire Rate}_\text{Burst} = \frac{ \text{Burst Count} }{ \frac{1}{\text{Modded Fire Rate}} + [ (\text{Burst Count} - 1) \cdot \text{Burst Delay} ] }
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
For Burst trigger types, there is a delay between bursts (Fire Rate value) and a delay between shots in a burst (Burst Delay value). For Mag Burst attacks, use the full magazine size as the Burst Count. For non-Burst attacks, you can set Burst Count = 1 (can think of shooting a whole magazine as a single "burst" regardless of trigger type) which resolves to Effective Fire Rate = Modded Fire Rate.
|-
|}

====Number of Shots Per Magazine====
Actual magazine size is needed to calculate sustained DPS.

{| class="wikitable"
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of Shots Per Magazine} &= \frac{ \text{Modded Mag Size} }{ \text{Ammo Cost Per Shot} }
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
Not all weapons consume one ammo per shot; this formula is needed to account for [[Continuous Weapon]]s and certain alt-fires
|-
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of Shots Per Magazine}_{Incarnon} &= \text{Max Incarnon Charge}
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
For [[Incarnon Form]], use Max Incarnon Charge. Ammo Cost is 1 per shot
|-
|}

====Average Sustained DPS====
Average sustained DPS is the theoretical damage a player does over an extended period of time, accounting time spent reloading/not firing their weapon.

{| class="wikitable"
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Proportion of Time Spent Shooting vs. Reloading} &= \frac{ \text{Number of Shots Per Mag} }{ \text{Effective Fire Rate} \times \text{Modded Reload Time} + \text{Number of Shots Per Mag}}
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
This ratio is a damage multiplier to multiply Burst DPS into Sustained DPS
*For the {{Weapon|Vectis}} and {{Weapon|Vectis Prime}} specifically, one (1) should be subtracted from the denominator to account for their lack of a [[reload]] delay.
*For {{Weapon|Epitaph}} specifically, ignore Modded Reload Time since it draws ammo directly from the full ammo pool similar to bows, but does not "reload" between shots like them.
*Reload time is in seconds.
*Reload time includes reload delay which is more prevalent for [[Battery Weapon]]s. Reload delay for most weapons are negligible if not non-existent.
|-
|
<math>
{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Average Sustained DPS} &= \text{Average Burst DPS} \times \text{Proportion of Time Spent Shooting vs. Reloading}
\end{aligned}
}
</math>
|
*Assumes that damage ramp up is at max for [[Continuous Weapon]]s. In actual gameplay, reloading will reset/decay the damage ramp up so Burst DPS will be lower than theoretical calculations.
|-
|}

===Damage Over Time===
{{Anchor|Damage Over Time Final Calculations}}
{{Main|Damage over Time}}

Damage-over-time tick damage is not subject to the 1/32 damage-type [[#Quantization|quantization]] described above. A proc is calculated from the attack's modded base damage rather than from the sum of its quantized damage-type values. Critical DoTs use the effective critical multiplier of the inducing hit; exact calculations should apply the critical multiplier quantization described on [[Critical Hit]].

For exact calculations, intermediate DoT operations use [[wikipedia:Single-precision floating-point format|binary32]] arithmetic.

For weapon-generated {{D|Heat}}, {{D|Electricity}}, {{D|Toxin}}, {{D|Gas}}, and {{D|Slash}} status effects, the temporary damage accumulator for each tick group starts at 1 rather than 0. The full-precision damage seeds are then added to this accumulator before the status coefficient and the remaining applicable multipliers are applied:
:<math>\text{Unrounded Tick Damage} = \left(\sum_i S_i + 1\right) \times C \times M</math>
Here, <math>S_i</math> is each stored damage seed, <math>C</math> is 0.5 for Heat, Electricity, Toxin, and Gas or 0.35 for Slash, and <math>M</math> is the product of the remaining applicable modifiers, such as elemental, faction, and status-damage bonuses. If several seeds are consolidated into a single tick, they are added to the same accumulator, so its initial value of 1 is included only once. It is therefore neither a final flat +1 damage bonus nor a bonus applied once per status stack.

Examples, before target defenses:
* {{D|Heat}}: {{Weapon|Supra Vandal}} has <math>40</math> base damage. With {{M|Thermite Rounds}} (+60% Heat damage), <math>(40 + 1) \times 0.5 \times 1.6 = 32.8</math>, displayed as <math>33</math>.
* {{D|Electricity}} with a <math>40</math> seed and +150% Electricity damage: <math>(40 + 1) \times 0.5 \times 2.5 = 51.25</math>, displayed as <math>51</math>.
* {{D|Toxin}} with a <math>40</math> seed, +225% Toxin damage, and {{M|Primed Bane of Orokin}} (+55% faction damage): <math>(40 \times 1.55 + 1) \times 0.5 \times 3.25 \times 1.55 = 158.68</math>, displayed as <math>159</math>.
* {{D|Gas}} with a <math>40</math> seed and no applicable bonuses: <math>(40 + 1) \times 0.5 = 20.5</math>, displayed as <math>21</math>.
* {{D|Slash}} with a <math>40</math> seed and {{M|Primed Bane of Orokin}} (+55% faction damage): <math>(40 \times 1.55 + 1) \times 0.35 \times 1.55 = 34.18</math>, displayed as <math>34</math>.

* {{D|Gas}} with nine consolidated stacks—six critical seeds of <math>80.0195389</math> and three non-critical seeds of <math>40</math>: using binary32 operations, <math>(6 \times 80.0195389 + 3 \times 40 + 1) \times 0.5 = 300.558594</math>, displayed as <math>301</math>. The fixed value of 1 is added once after summing the seeds, not once per stack.
* {{D|Heat}} accumulates active stacks into one tick. With +60% Heat damage, one <math>40</math> seed and one <math>80.0195389</math> seed produce <math>(40 + 80.0195389 + 1) \times 0.5 \times 1.6 = 96.8156357</math>, displayed as <math>97</math>.
* {{D|Electricity}} proc instances keep their own durations, but contributions occurring on the same pulse are consolidated into one damage number. With +150% Electricity damage, the same two seeds produce <math>(40 + 80.0195389 + 1) \times 0.5 \times 2.5 = 151.274429</math>, displayed as <math>151</math>.
* {{D|Slash}} and {{D|Toxin}} stacks tick independently and display separate damage numbers; only up to 10 tick numbers of each status are shown. Consequently, each stack uses its own fixed value of 1. For example, separate {{D|Slash}} stacks with seeds of <math>40</math> and <math>80.0195389</math> deal <math>(40 + 1) \times 0.35 = 14.35</math> and <math>(80.0195389 + 1) \times 0.35 = 28.3568382</math>, displayed separately as <math>14</math> and <math>28</math>.

After all applicable multipliers and target defenses are applied, damage pop-ups present the result as a whole number. For non-negative raw damage values, the displayed number is:
:<math>\text{Displayed Damage} = \left\lfloor \text{Raw Damage} + 0.5 \right\rfloor</math>
This is a display-formatting rule only; it does not imply that the underlying raw damage value or the target's health change is rounded to an integer. The fixed value of 1 in the status formula above is part of the raw damage calculation and is unrelated to display rounding.

{{D|Blast}} are not a damage-over-time (DoT) effect but a stack-and-detonate effect, so the per-tick DoT formula above does not apply and there is no DoT "+1" starting value. As with DoT, Blast's intermediate operations use binary32 (f32) arithmetic.

* '''Stacking:''' each Blast proc adds one stack, up to 10 (bosses and eximus-type enemies cap at 4). Each stack lasts 1.5 seconds and records the damage ''H'' of the hit that applied it.
* '''Stack expiry:''' if a stack expires on its own (1.5 s) instead of being consumed by a detonation, it deals a single instance of max(1, 0.3 × ''H'') Blast damage.
* '''Detonation:''' once stacks reach the cap (10; bosses 4), or the enemy dies at any stack count, the currently active stacks are not settled individually but are combined into a single 5-meter radial Blast centered on the enemy, dealing 3 × (sum of the active stacks' ''H''). This radial has no distance falloff within 5 m, and the stacks are cleared afterward. Death detonation likewise uses the fixed ×3 and does not scale with the current stack count.

===Lifetime Damage===
Lifetime damage is a derived damage stat that is based on the total amount of damage that a weapon can deal before it depletes its ammo reserve. [[Melee]] weapons, [[Battery Weapon]]s or rechargable weapons, and [[Exalted Weapon]]s (assuming [[Energy]] is always restored) will deal infinite damage over their in-game use since they are always available and are not reliant on [[Pickups|ammo pickups]] or [[Squad Ammo Restore]]s.

\end{aligned}

The average total damage dealt by a weapon without switching weapons or replenishing ammo.
